About the Role As an FPGA Engineer Intern on Harmattan AI’s compute module team, you will take camera aggregation from concept to real hardware for the first time. Our drones carry more cameras than a single processor can take in, and your job is to show how an FPGA can close that gap. You will own the work end to end, from first design to a demonstrator on the bench. Your results will set how cameras are connected in our next hardware generation. Responsibilities Integrate existing IP cores, write HDL wrappers, simulate and validate FPGA logic that merges multiple camera streams into one. Investigate the system’s limits in camera count, resolution and frame rate. Build the processor-side pipeline that splits the merged stream so each camera stays independently usable. Debug the full chain, from cables and connectors to FPGA logic and camera software on the processor. Deliver a complete demonstrator and documentation that guide our next hardware design. Candidate Requirements Final-year Master’s or engineering school student in electrical engineering, electronics or embedded systems. Previous hands-on experience with FPGAs and digital board design and debugging. Experience writing software that runs close to the hardware; embedded Linux is a plus. Ideally, previous exposure to video or camera interfaces. Hands-on in the lab and comfortable reworking wiring, connectors and test setups to get a system running.
